we present a new learning framework, GSL, which allows for a novel family of loss functions that can be used to learn a generative model.
our proposed learning framework and model are able to synthesize novel examples with high quality, even if no example of the new attribute is witnessed during training.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we propose an objective function that allows neural networks to envision visual objects with different attributes.
we propose a novel learning framework, termed Group-Supervised learning (GSL), and an implementation based on an autoencoder termed Group-Supervised Zero-Shot Synthesis Network (GZSNet).
we introduce a new learning framework, Group-Supervised learning, that allows for the disentanglement and recombination of components of an input.
The main takeaway from our work is that
GSL can be used for zero-shot generation of novel samples that are not witnessed during training.
GSL provides a general framework for zero-shot synthesis that can be applied to a wide range of tasks.
GSL allows neural networks to envision novel objects, in the absence of examples of the object, by leveraging the ability of the networks to generalize from examples of similar objects.
